stances.note: Russian-occupied regions of Ukraine (Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson) has not written its reading of Ukraine; the atlas mirrors Ukraine's 'claimed territory' reading as 'rival' at low confidence, on the same evidence. Bond and trend are not assessed from this side.

stances_toward.note: Proclaimed annexed on 30 Sep 2022 (Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson) and claimed in full, though at the start of 2026 Russia held 99.6%, 78%, 75% and 72% respectively. The unoccupied rest of Donetsk is the price Moscow sets for peace: the Kremlin demands a Ukrainian withdrawal before any settlement, and the 28-point plan of Nov 2025 wrote it in as a demilitarised zone recognised as de facto Russian. Graded own territory because the Kremlin's map treats the oblasts as subjects of the Federation; the part not controlled is the war aim. Bond - kin.

stances_toward.note: Luhansk (99.6% occupied), Donetsk (78%), Zaporizhzhia (75%) and Kherson (72%) at the start of 2026 (DeepState); Russia proclaimed their annexation on 30 Sep 2022 and the General Assembly rejected it on 12 Oct 2022. The unoccupied rest of Donetsk (Sloviansk-Kramatorsk) is the sticking point: the Kremlin demands a Ukrainian withdrawal as the condition of peace, Kyiv refuses. Ukraine's map shows these oblasts as claimed, not controlled; the part still under Ukrainian control is own territory and is not drawn separately.

relations_to.summary: Tokayev said at the St Petersburg forum on 17 Jun 2022, beside Putin, that Kazakhstan does not recognise the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' ('quasi-state formations'), citing the same principle as for Taiwan, Kosovo, Abkhazia and South Ossetia; the foreign ministry has not recognised the later annexations. Zelensky thanked him. Putin suspended a Kazakh oil shipment via Novorossiysk the next day (reported).
